name: Blinatumomab (3, 4 day) Protocol
full_name: Blinatumomab for Philadelphia-chromosome-negative relapsed or refractory B-precursor Acute Lymphoblastic Leukaemia (3, 4 day schedule)
indication: Treatment of Philadelphia-chromosome-negative relapsed or refractory B-precursor acute lymphoblastic leukaemia.

drugs.special_instructions: Continuous intravenous infusion in 240ml sodium chloride 0.9% at a rate of 2.5ml/hour via a pump. Each bag contains sufficient volume and drug for a 96-hour infusion, although administered over alternate 72 and 96 hours. 9 mcg/day dose: 41.25 mcg in 275ml total; 28 mcg/day dose: 133.75 mcg in 275ml total. NOTE: Cycle 1 Days 1-7: 9 mcg/day step-up dose. Cycle 1 Days 8-28 and all of Cycles 2-5: 28 mcg/day. ARIA administers the first, third, fifth and seventh infusions of each cycle over 72 hours (must start on a Monday, Tuesday or Friday); the second, fourth, sixth and eighth infusions are administered over 96 hours. Central venous access, dedicated lumen required. Administer through a Polyolefin, PVC non-DEHP, or EVA intravenous infusion line with a low protein-binding 0.2µm in-line filter. Do not flush infusion lines into the patient — this will cause an inadvertent bolus of blinatumomab. The line must be replaced with every change of infusion bag. Administration period must not exceed 28 days in total in any given cycle. Days of administration may need to be adjusted on ARIA depending on the time of the Day 1 infusion start.

pre_medications.special_instructions: 20mg or equivalent dose intravenous, 60 minutes prior to Day 1 blinatumomab infusion on every cycle.

Administer 60 minutes before start of blinatumomab infusion on Day 1 of every cycle. Check if the patient has already taken paracetamol — maximum dose is 4000mg per 24 hours. Continue paracetamol 1000mg four times a day for first 48 hours (Days 1 and 2) to help reduce pyrexia.

take_home_medicines.special_instructions: Then 1000mg four times a day as required for pyrexia during the first 48 hours of each cycle.
For Cycle 1 only. For prevention of Tumour Lysis Syndrome. Aggressive hydration also recommended.

take_home_medicines.frequency: Once a day on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays only

rescue_medications.special_instructions: When required for relief of infusion related reactions.
When required for relief of infusion related reactions.
Range 12.5-25mg IV. For the relief of rigors following verbal confirmation from a doctor. The regimen summary standardises to 25mg; 12.5mg may be used as starting dose.
When required for relief of infusion related reactions.

drugs.special_instructions: Cycle 1 step-up dose: 9 mcg/day continuous intravenous infusion in 240ml sodium chloride 0.9% at 2.5ml/hour via a pump (Days 1-7). Bag contains 41.25mcg in 275ml total. Administered on Day 1 over 72 hours, then Day 4 over 96 hours. ARIA administers the first, third, fifth and seventh infusions over 72 hours; second, fourth, sixth and eighth over 96 hours. Central venous access, dedicated lumen required. Do not flush infusion lines into the patient. Replace line with every bag change.

Cycle 1 full dose: 28 mcg/day continuous intravenous infusion in 240ml sodium chloride 0.9% at 2.5ml/hour via a pump (Days 8-28). Bag contains 133.75mcg in 275ml total. Bags changed on Days 8, 11, 15, 18, 22, 25, alternating 72 and 96 hours. ARIA administers the first, third, fifth and seventh infusions over 72 hours; second, fourth, sixth and eighth over 96 hours. Central venous access, dedicated lumen required. Do not flush infusion lines into the patient. Replace line with every bag change.

special_instructions: Cycle 1: step-up dosing — 9mcg/day Days 1-7, then 28mcg/day Days 8-28.
42-day cycle (28 days infusion + 14 days treatment-free interval).
Patient should remain in-patient for first 9 days of cycle 1.
Bag change schedule: Day 1 (72h run), Day 4 (96h run), Day 8 (72h run), Day 11 (96h run), Day 15 (72h run), Day 18 (96h run), Day 22 (72h run), Day 25 (96h run). Total 8 bags per cycle.

drugs.special_instructions: Cycles 2-5: 28 mcg/day continuous intravenous infusion in 240ml sodium chloride 0.9% at 2.5ml/hour via a pump for all 28 days (no step-up). Bag contains 133.75mcg in 275ml total. Bags changed on Days 1, 4, 8, 11, 15, 18, 22, 25, alternating 72 and 96 hours. ARIA administers the first, third, fifth and seventh infusions over 72 hours; second, fourth, sixth and eighth over 96 hours. Central venous access, dedicated lumen required. Do not flush infusion lines into the patient. Replace line with every bag change.

special_instructions: 42-day cycle (28 days infusion + 14 days treatment-free interval).
Patient should remain in-patient for at least 2 days of cycle 2.
Bag change schedule: Day 1 (72h run), Day 4 (96h run), Day 8 (72h run), Day 11 (96h run), Day 15 (72h run), Day 18 (96h run), Day 22 (72h run), Day 25 (96h run). Total 8 bags per cycle.

dose_modifications.condition: Cytokine Release Syndrome / Tumour Lysis Syndrome NCI-CTC Grade 3
dose_modifications.description: Interrupt blinatumomab until resolved, then restart at 9 mcg/day. Escalate to 28 mcg/day after 7 days if the toxicity does not recur.
dose_modifications.action_text: Interrupt blinatumomab (CRS/TLS Grade 3) — restart at 9mcg/day, escalate to 28mcg/day after 7 days if no recurrence

dose_modifications.condition: Cytokine Release Syndrome / Tumour Lysis Syndrome NCI-CTC Grade 4
Neurological toxicity: more than one convulsion
Neurological toxicity: NCI-CTC Grade 3, resolved to Grade 1 (mild) for at least 3 days
dose_modifications.description: Interrupt blinatumomab until no more than grade 1 (mild) and for at least 3 days, then restart blinatumomab at 9 mcg/day. Escalate to 28 mcg/day after 7 days if the toxicity does not recur. On re-initiation, pre-medicate with a 24mg dose of dexamethasone. Then reduce dexamethasone step-wise over 4 days.
dose_modifications.action_text: Interrupt blinatumomab (Neuro Grade 3) — restart at 9mcg/day with dexamethasone 24mg pre-med

dose_modifications.condition: Neurological toxicity: NCI-CTC Grade 3, occurred at 9 mcg/day OR takes more than 7 days to resolve
dose_modifications.action_text: Discontinue blinatumomab permanently (Neuro Grade 3 at 9mcg/day or >7 days to resolve)

dose_modifications.description: If clinically relevant, interrupt blinatumomab until no more than grade 1 (mild), then restart blinatumomab at 9 mcg/day. Escalate to 28 mcg/day after 7 days if the toxicity does not recur.
dose_modifications.action_text: Interrupt blinatumomab (Liver enzymes Grade 3) — restart at 9mcg/day, escalate to 28mcg/day after 7 days
Consider discontinuing blinatumomab permanently (Liver enzymes Grade 4)

dose_modifications.condition: Other clinically relevant adverse reactions: NCI-CTC Grade 3
dose_modifications.description: Interrupt blinatumomab until no more than grade 1 (mild), then restart blinatumomab at 9 mcg/day. Escalate to 28 mcg/day after 7 days if the toxicity does not recur.
dose_modifications.action_text: Interrupt blinatumomab (Other toxicity Grade 3) — restart at 9mcg/day

dose_modifications.condition: Other clinically relevant adverse reactions: NCI-CTC Grade 4
dose_modifications.action_text: Consider discontinuing blinatumomab permanently (Other toxicity Grade 4)

dose_modifications.condition: Treatment interrupted for more than four hours
dose_modifications.description: Patient should be examined by a healthcare professional. If interruption after an adverse event is ≤ 7 days, continue the same cycle to a total of 28 days of infusion. If interruption > 7 days, start a new cycle. If toxicity takes more than 14 days to resolve, discontinue blinatumomab permanently (unless specified otherwise in the table).
dose_modifications.action_text: Re-evaluate blinatumomab (interruption >4 hours): ≤7 days continue cycle; >7 days new cycle; >14 days discontinue

dose_modifications.description: No dose modifications for haematological toxicity are necessary for blinatumomab. If treatment with blinatumomab is not tolerated it should be stopped.
dose_modifications.action_text: No haematological dose modification required. Stop if not tolerated.

monitoring: FBC, U&Es and LFTs on day 1 of each cycle.
Hepatitis B, C and HIV serology prior to cycle one.
Neurological examination prior to starting therapy and clinical monitoring for signs/symptoms of neurologic events (e.g., writing test) during treatment.
Close monitoring for signs or symptoms of Cytokine Release Syndrome (CRS), especially during initiation of first and second treatment cycles and first 48 hours.
Close monitoring for signs or symptoms of Tumour Lysis Syndrome (TLS), including renal function and fluid balance in the first 48 hours after the first infusion.
warnings: Blinatumomab is a set dose and does not require dose banding.
Dosing errors have been observed with blinatumomab treatment. It is very important that administration instructions are strictly followed.
The administration period must not exceed 28 days in total in any given cycle.
Central venous access is required. Infuse through a dedicated lumen.
Administer blinatumomab through a Polyolefin, PVC non-DEHP, or EVA intravenous infusion line with a low protein-binding 0.2µm in-line filter.
Do not flush infusion lines into the patient, as it will cause an inadvertent bolus of blinatumomab. The line must be replaced with every change of the infusion bag.
Patients with evidence of impaired renal function should be carefully monitored as they are prone to additional myelosuppression.

Counsel patients on potential neurologic effects and advise patients not to drive, use heavy machinery, or engage in hazardous activities while on treatment and to promptly report any neurological symptoms.
Gastric protection (proton pump inhibitor or H2 antagonist) may be considered in patients considered at high risk of GI ulceration or bleed.
Patients should be encouraged to drink at least three litres of fluid per 24 hours.
Cycle one and two are started in the hospital setting. It is recommended the patient remain an in-patient for the first 9 days of cycle one and at least two days of cycle two.
Consider pre-phase corticosteroid treatment prior to cycle 1 if peripheral blast count >15% or bone marrow blasts >50%. This is not prescribed on ARIA and must be managed separately.
Take-home (supportive) medicines have been included in this protocol. If an in-patient stay is necessary, these must also be prescribed on the in-patient chart.
The days of administration may need to be adjusted on ARIA depending on the time of the Day 1 infusion start. Treatment must start on a Monday, Tuesday or Friday.

TLS prophylaxis: appropriate prophylactic measures including aggressive hydration and anti-hyperuricaemic therapy (allopurinol or rasburicase) should be used, especially in patients with higher leukocytosis or a high tumour burden.
CRS: premedication with dexamethasone is intended to prevent CRS. Median time to onset of a CRS event was 2 days. Monitor closely especially during first and second cycles.
